method: CPU torch.load metadata only; no gameplay or network evaluation. Best legacy evaluation is selected within each saved checkpoint history. Scores use already-inspected legacy evaluation boards and may have different game counts, so they are not held-out comparisons.

negative_safe_cost_bound.sufficient_condition: For safe=-c<=0 and 0<=gamma<1, c/(1-gamma)<=mine is sufficient to keep negative returns >=-mine.
negative_safe_cost_bound.reason: After N safe clicks followed by a mine, the negative component is -c*(1-gamma**N)/(1-gamma)-gamma**N*mine, a convex combination of -c/(1-gamma) and -mine. Positive reveal/late/burst payments cannot lower this.
negative_safe_cost_bound.implementation_recommendation: In phase2 allow these bounded negative-safe cases, or derive full finite-horizon bounds. Current conservative guard does not affect the13 queued safe0 candidates. Gamma1 and positive flat safe rewards need separate bounds.

phase2_notes.training_provenance: wall3/wall4 used skip_coin_flips=True: solver-based reward/replay filtering. This is different from the current outcome-only training protocol, even though inference remains board-only. stage3m40 predates this option; easy-progress explicitly disabled it.
phase2_notes.legacy_selection: Do not treat a selected best score on repeatedly used legacy boards as proof of superiority. Model evaluation at saved checkpoint is stored separately from maximum earlier history; easy-flat exemplifies the distinction.
